facts.statement: Nasutoceratops is classified as a basal member of the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops was a basal (early diverging) member of Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: The function of the deep front of the Nasutoceratops skull is unknown but may be related to mastication.
facts.quote: The function of the deep front of the skull of Nasutoceratops is unknown, but may have been related to mastication

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the forward-oriented brow horns may have enabled interlocking with opponents, similar to modern bovids.
facts.quote: The forward oriented brow horns of Nasutoceratops may have enabled interlocking with opponents, as in modern bovids

facts.statement: One of three new ceratopsian taxa was identified from a locality discovered by Eric K. Lund during the 2006 field season.
facts.quote: Among the discoveries that have been made are three new ceratopsian (horned dinosaur) taxa, one of which was identified from UMNH Locality VP 940 discovered by the then graduate student and technician Eric K. Lund during the 2006 field season

facts.statement: Three specimens were collected: UMNH VP 16800 in 2006, and UMNH VP 19469 and UMNH VP 19466 in later years.
facts.quote: Three specimens of this dinosaur were collected; UMNH VP 16800 in 2006, and UMNH VP 19469 and UMNH VP 19466 in subsequent years

facts.statement: Scott D. Sampson, Eric K. Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, and Katherine E. Clayton named Nasutoceratops titusi in 2013.
facts.quote: The paleontologists Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, and Katherine E. Clayton briefly described and scientifically named the new genus and species Nasutoceratops titusi in 2013

facts.statement: The holotype was collected with an articulated left forelimb, a fragmentary right forelimb, parts of the pectoral girdle, neck and back vertebrae, and three patches of skin impressions on the left forelimb.
facts.quote: It was collected with an articulated and almost complete left forelimb, an associated yet very fragmentary right forelimb (both lacking hand bones), much of the pectoral girdle, an almost complete syncervical vertebra (the three first neck vertebrae fused together), three associated but fragmentary dorsal vertebrae (of the back), as well as three patches of skin impressions associated with the left forelimb

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was a large-bodied, quadrupedal dinosaur with a huge skull, hooked beak, heavy skeleton, shortened tail, large pelvis, and short digits.
facts.quote: As a centrosaurine ceratopsid, it would have been a large bodied, quadrupedal dinosaur with a huge skull, a hooked upper beak, a heavily constructed skeleton, a shortened, down-swept tail, a large pelvis indicating powerful muscles, and short digits

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops had three horns: one nasal horn above the nasal opening and two brow horns above the eye sockets.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops had three horns; the nasal horn above the nasal opening and the brow horns above the eye sockets

facts.statement: The snout region of Nasutoceratops is almost circular and expands upwards to give a bulbous appearance, resembling the basal centrosaurine Diabloceratops rather than more derived centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The snout region is almost circular overall, which is typical of centrosaurines, but it differs from more derived (or "advanced") centrosaurines and is more similar to the basal (early diverging) Diabloceratops in that it expands upwards, giving the snout region a bulbous appearance.

facts.statement: The snout of Nasutoceratops is short due to abbreviated nasal and maxilla bones and may be the shortest of any centrosaurine.
facts.quote: The shortness of the snout is a result of the abbreviated nasal and maxilla bones, and it may be the shortest of any centrosaurine.

facts.statement: Although the rostral bone is not preserved, it is inferred to have been triangular in side view, a feature similar to centrosaurines and unlike chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: The rostral (a bone unique to ceratopsians, which forms the upper beak and contacts the front part of the premaxilla) is not preserved in Nasutoceratops, but by inferring from the contact area of the premaxilla behind it, it has been interpreted as triangular in side view, similar to centrosaurines and unlike chasmosaurines (the other main group of ceratopsids).

facts.statement: Each maxilla of Nasutoceratops is estimated to have contained 29 teeth, though it remains undetermined if they were double-rooted or single-rooted.
facts.quote: Each maxilla is estimated to have contained 29 teeth, but it has not been determined whether they were double-rooted as in other ceratopsids or single-rooted as in neoceratopsians.

facts.statement: The nasal horn core of Nasutoceratops is low, long, and blade-like with a teardrop-shaped expansion at the front.
facts.quote: The nasal horn core that formed the bony part of the horn above the nasal opening is low, long, and blade-like, pinched from side to side along the hind part, and with a somewhat raised, teardrop-shaped expansion at the front.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Nasutoceratops have well-developed internal cavities suggesting they were hollow and possibly pneumatized, a feature unknown in other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The nasal bones have well-developed internal cavities behind the horn, which suggests they were hollow, and possibly pneumatized (air-filled); pneumatic nasals are unknown in other ceratopsians.

facts.statement: The skull roof of Nasutoceratops is very vaulted around the eye region, giving the impression of a forward-facing forehead similar to Diabloceratops, Albertaceratops, and many chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: The skull roof is very vaulted around the eye region, which gives the impression that Nasutoceratops had a forward facing "forehead" across its width, similar to Diabloceratops and Albertaceratops, as well as many chasmosaurines.

facts.statement: The skull frill of Nasutoceratops is nearly circular, with its maximum width located in the middle region.
facts.quote: The frill is almost circular with its widest point at the middle region.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops possesses two large, oval openings in its frill, a feature typical of centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The frill has two large, oval parietal fenestrae, one on each parietal, as is typical for centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Unlike most centrosaurines, the frill of Nasutoceratops lacked well-developed hooks and spikes.
facts.quote: The frill lacked the well-developed hooks and spikes that are otherwise typical for centrosaurines.

facts.statement: Researchers consider it unlikely that Nasutoceratops developed hooks and spikes as it matured, despite the holotype being immature.
facts.quote: Since the holotype was not fully grown, it is possible such hooks would have developed as it matured, but this is considered unlikely due to the fusion of its epiparietals on the frill and fusion of other bones related to maturity.

facts.statement: The humerus of Nasutoceratops is 475 mm long, with a deltopectoral crest covering nearly half its length.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) is 475 mm long, and has a hemispheric humeral head (upper part) and prominent deltopectoral crest, which accounts for of almost half the whole length of the humerus, as common for the group.

facts.statement: The ulna of Nasutoceratops measures 400 mm in length and features a large olecranon process for triceps muscle attachment.
facts.quote: The ulna (one of two lower arm bones) is 400 mm long and has a large olecranon process where the triceps muscle inserted.

facts.statement: Skin impressions on the left forelimb of the Nasutoceratops holotype reveal three distinct patterns of tubercle-shaped scales.
facts.quote: The three patches with skin impressions that are associated with the scapula and humerus of the left forelimb of the holotype are preserved both as casts and molds, and show three kinds of patterns formed by tubercle (round nodule) shaped scales.

facts.statement: The most notable skin impression on Nasutoceratops consists of raised hexagonal tubercles 8-11 mm in diameter surrounded by triangular grooves.
facts.quote: Patch C, the most notable impression, consists of raised, hexagonal tubercles that measure 8-11 mm in diameter, and are surrounded by triangular grooves.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nasutoceratops would have developed typical centrosaurine hooks and spikes if it had reached full maturity.
facts.quote: Since the holotype was not fully grown, it is possible such hooks would have developed as it matured, but this is considered unlikely due to the fusion of its epiparietals on the frill and fusion of other bones related to maturity.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was assigned to the subfamily Centrosaurinae by Sampson and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops was assigned to Centrosaurinae by Sampson and colleagues in 2013

facts.statement: Researchers named a new clade Nasutoceratopsini with Nasutoceratops as the type genus.
facts.quote: These authors named this new clade Nasutoceratopsini, with Nasutoceratops as the type genus

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis suggested that Nasutoceratopsini did not form a monophyletic group.
facts.quote: The 2021 phylogenetic analysis by Dalman and colleagues accompanying the description of the basal centrosaurine Menefeeceratops from the Menefee Formation of New Mexico did not result in Nasutoceratopsini forming a monophyletic (natural) group

facts.statement: A 2023 analysis by Ishikawa and colleagues recovered Nasutoceratopsini as a natural, basal group.
facts.quote: The paleontologist Hiroki Ishikawa and colleagues did recover Nasutoceratopsini as a natural, basal group in their 2023 analysis

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops belongs to the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous Campanian stage, between 75.9 and 75.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, durante el Campaniano, entre 75.9 a 75.5 millones de años

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que ahora es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was a large, quadrupedal herbivore with a short snout and unique rounded horns over its eyes.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops era un herbívoro cuadrúpedo grande, con un hocico corto y cuernos redondeados únicos sobre sus ojos

facts.statement: The horns of Nasutoceratops extended almost to the tip of its snout and are the longest among all members of the Centrosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Extendiéndose casi hasta la punta de su hocico, estos cuernos son los más largos de todos los miembros de la subfamilia de los Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops possessed pneumatic elements in its nasal bones, a trait unknown in any other ceratopsian.
facts.quote: La presencia de elementos neumáticos en los huesos nasales de Nasutoceratops es un rasgo único y se desconoce en cualquier otra ceratópsido

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops, Diabloceratops, and Machairoceratops are the only three known centrosaurine dinosaurs from the southwestern United States.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops, Diabloceratops y Machairoceratops son los únicos tres dinosaurios centrosaurinídos del suroeste de Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Researchers cautioned that more material, particularly parietal bones, is needed to determine the position of nasutoceratopsins near the base of Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: They cautioned that more material, especially parietal bones, was needed to determine the position of potential nasutoceratopsins near the base of Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: The body length of Nasutoceratops is estimated at 4.5 meters and its weight at 1.5 tons.
facts.quote: La longitud de su cuerpo se ha estimado en 4.5 metros, su peso en 1.5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The snout area around the nasal fossa is strongly developed, representing nearly three-quarters of the skull length relative to the eye sockets.
facts.quote: La parte del hocico alrededor de la fosa nasal está fuertemente desarrollada, representando cerca de tres cuartos de la longitud del cráneo frente a las cuencas de los ojos.

facts.statement: The posterior part of each nasal bone is hollowed out by a large internal cavity.
facts.quote: La parte posterior de cada hueso nasal está ahuecada por una gran cavidad interna.

facts.statement: The brow horns point forward and outward at their bases, then curve inward and finally twist their tips upward.
facts.quote: Los cuernos de las cejas en sus bases apuntan hacia adelante y hacia afuera, luego se curvan hacia adentro y finalmente tuercen sus puntos hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The nasal horn is low and narrow with an elongated base.
facts.quote: El cuerno en la nariz es bajo y estrecho, con una base alargada.

facts.statement: The squamosal has a high crest on its upper surface extending from the eye socket direction to the squamosal edge.
facts.quote: El escamoso tiene una cresta alta en su superficie superior, que va desde la dirección de la cuenca del ojo hacia el borde escamoso.

facts.statement: The osteoderms on the frill edge, epiparietals, and episquamosals are not spike-shaped but resemble simple low half-moons.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos en el borde del volante, los epiparietales y los episquamosales, no tienen forma de espigas, sino que tienen la forma de simples medias lunas bajas.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops had up to 29 tooth positions in the upper jaw, each occupied by several stacked teeth.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops tenía hasta 29 posiciones de dientes en el maxilar, cada una ocupada por varios dientes apilados.

facts.statement: The epijugal, the cheek bone, has a length of 85 millimeters, also the largest known among centrosaurines.
facts.quote: El epiyugal, el hueso de las mejillas, tiene una longitud de 85 milímetros, también el más grande conocido entre los centrosaurinídos.

facts.statement: The skull frill is moderately long and perforated by a large kidney-shaped parietal fenestra on each side.
facts.quote: El volante del cráneo es moderadamente largo y perforado por una gran fenestra parietal en forma de riñón a cada lado.

facts.statement: In the forelimb, the ulna is exceptionally robust with a large olecranon process.
facts.quote: En la extremidad anterior, el cúbito es excepcionalmente robusto con un gran proceso de olécranon.

facts.statement: Remains of Nasutoceratops were found in Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en Utah, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The species is known from the holotype UMNH VP 16800, an almost complete skull found in association with a left forelimb, partial anterior dorsal vertebrae, a synsacrum, a pectoral girdle, parts of the right forelimb, and skin impressions, plus referred materials including an adult disarticulated skull (UMNH VP 19466) and an isolated squamosal (UMNH VP 19469).
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir del holotipo UMNH VP 16800, un cráneo casi completo encontrado en asociación y una extremidad izquierda también asociada, tres vértebras dorsales anterior parciales, una sincervical, una cintura escapular, partes de la extremidad anterior derecha e impresiones de la piel y de los materiales referidos UMNH VP 19466, un cráneo adulto desarticulado que consiste en una premaxila, maxilar y nasal incompletas y UMNH VP 19469, un hueso escamoso aislado.

facts.statement: It was discovered and collected in the Kaiparowits Basin Project, started by the University of Utah in 2000, in the middle unit of the Kaiparowits Formation within the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto y recolectado en el Proyecto Cuenca Kaiparowits, iniciado por la Universidad de Utah en 2000, en la unidad media de la Formación Kaiparowits dentro del Monumento Nacional Grand Staircase-Escalante.

facts.statement: It was originally named by Eric Karl Lund, Scott D. Sampson, and Mark A. Loewen in 2011 as "Nasutuceratops" but was not officially published, making it a nomen ex dissertatione without validity.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado originalmente por Eric Karl Lund, Scott D. Sampson y Mark A. Loewen en el año de 2011 como "Nasutuceratops", pero aún sin publicarse de manera oficial, por lo que era un nomen ex dissertatione sin validez.

facts.statement: Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, and Katherine E. Clayton published it officially in 2013, correcting the genus name to Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: Scott D. Sampson, Lund, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke y Katherine E. Clayton realizaron su publicación oficial en 2013, corrigiendo el nombre de género a Nasutoceratops.

facts.statement: The species name honors Alan L. Titus for recovering the Nasutoceratops fossils from the GSENM.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a Alan L. Titus por recuperar los fósiles de Nasutuceratops del GSENM.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures approximately 1.5 to 1.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo del holotipo mide aproximadamente entre 1.5 a 1.8 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops was assigned to the Centrosaurinae in 2013 in a relatively basal position.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops fue asignado a los Centrosaurinae en 2013, en una posición relativamente basal.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. in 2013 discovered that Nasutoceratops was the sister taxon of Avaceratops.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Sampson et al. en 2013 descubrió que Nasutoceratops era el taxón hermano de Avaceratops.

facts.statement: In 2016, this clade was named Nasutoceratopsini, containing Nasutoceratops, the holotype of Avaceratops (ANSP 15800), MOR 692, the newly described CMN 8804 from the Oldman Formation, and another undescribed ceratopsian found in Malta, Montana.
facts.quote: En 2016, este clado se llamó Nasutoceratopsini, el cual contiene a Nasutoceratops, así como ANSP 15800, el holotipo de Avaceratops, MOR 692, previamente tratado como un espécimen adulto de Avaceratops, el recién descrito CMN 8804 de la Formación Oldman y otro ceratopsio no descrito encontrado en Malta, Montana.

facts.statement: Argon-argon dating indicates the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La datación radiométrica de argón-argón indica que la Formación Kaiparowits fue depositada entre 76.1 y 74.0 millones de años atrás, durante la etapa del Campaniense del Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Kaiparowits Formation site was located near the western coast of the Niobrara Sea, a large inland sea that divided North America into two landmasses: Laramidia to the west and Appalachia to the east.
facts.quote: Durante el período Cretácico Superior, el sitio de la Formación Kaiparowits estaba ubicado cerca de la costa occidental del mar de Niobrara, un gran mar interior que dividió a América del Norte en dos masas de tierra, Laramidia al oeste y Appalachia hacia el este.

facts.statement: The plateau where the dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetlands, peat bogs, ponds, and lakes, and was surrounded by highlands.
facts.quote: La meseta donde vivían los dinosaurios era una antigua llanura de inundación dominada por grandes canales y abundantes humedales, pantanos de turba, estanques y lagos, y estaba rodeada de tierras altas.

facts.statement: The climate was humid and warm and supported a wide and diverse range of organisms.
facts.quote: El clima era húmedo y cálido y soportaba una amplia y diversa gama de organismos.

facts.statement: Nasutoceratops shared its paleoenvironment with theropods such as dromaeosaurids, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, ornithomimids like Ornithomimus velox, tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus and Teratophoneus, armored ankylosaurs, the duck-billed dinosaurs Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus and Gryposaurus monumentensis, the ceratopsians Utahceratops gettyi and Kosmoceratops richardsoni, and the oviraptorosaur Hagryphus giganteus.
facts.quote: Nasutoceratops compartió su paleoambiente con terópodos como dromeosáuridos, el troodóntido Talos sampsoni, ornitomímidos como Ornithomimus velox, tiranosáuridos como Albertosaurus y Teratophoneus, anquilosáuridos blindados, los dinosaurios pico de pato Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus y Gryposaurus monumentensis, los ceratópsidos Utahceratops gettyi y Kosmoceratops richardsoni y el ovirraptorosaurio Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: According to this study, the existence of Nasutoceratops would support the hypothesis of faunal separation between the north and south of Laramidia.
facts.quote: Según este estudio, la existencia de Nasutoceratops apoyaría la hipótesis de la separación de fauna entre el norte y el sur de Laramidia.
